downloads `punkt_tab` instead of `punkt` which has a critical security
vulnerability (CVE-2024-39705).

Changed method for getting the systems

Previously, the method get_matrix_add and get_matrix_mul
allowed to get the ansatz system for the usual computations.

Since the code was fairly similar to the building of the ansatz systems
for simple computations, we changed the meaning of these functions
allowing now to build systems of any size, inhomogenous or not. This
required a small adaptation of the methods
that computed the annihilating operator (the two steps method such as
_compute_add_solution) to include the
size of the system and the homogenous requirement.

These new methods need to be adapted in all inherited classes (like
fullLazyOperator).

commit message:
Added new guessing functionality

Added three new methods to toDiffAlgebraic.py
	- A method that, if y(x) = exp(int(u(x))), computes the differential polynomials
	U_n(u) such that y^(n)(x) = y(x)U_n(u). (Exponential_polynomials)
	- A method that, given an homogeneous differentially algebraic equation suppose
	that the solution is of the form y(x) = exp(int(u(x))) and computes a
	differentially algebraic equation for u(x) which will have less order than y(x).
	(simplify_homogeneous)
	- A method that, given an homogeneous differentially algebraic equation use the
	method simplify_homogeneous and in case that a linear equation is achieved, then
	a Dn-finite function is returned as an iteration of exponential functions
	(guess_homogeenous_DNfinite).

commit message:
Performance improvements

1 - The method for computing the root of the indicial polynomial now is cached.
This means that operators with the same indicial polynomial take less time to
compute their roots.
2 - Computing th roots of the indicial polynomial when there are parameters is done
using a modular approximation: we evaluate the parameters and when the polynomial
has the same degree we compute the roots of a univariate polynomial. That is a superset
of the roots we want, so we check and we keep those that were roots for the indicial polynomial.

Minor changes:
   matrix.py now use the method is_Matrix instead of sage.matrix.Matrix (deprecated in
SAGE: https://trac.sagemath.org/ticket/24096

commit message:
Merge pull request #24 from Antonio-JP/reorganize

**NOTE:** we force this pull request since it is the beginning of a refactor process.

This pull request incorporate a first reorganization of the code of `dd_functions` preserving its functionality but preparing the main refactoring that is to come for version 1.0.0.

* We have split the repository into 4 folders:
  - The code folder has been renamed from _ajpastor_ to _dd_functions_.
  - A new _notebooks_ folder has been created for all the notebooks in the repository
  - A new _experiments_ folder has been created to include different scripts using the package.
  - The code _docs_ keeps holding the compiled documentation using Sphinx.
* We have updated the CI actions for GitHub. Now it uses SageMath tool `tox` for linting and testing.
* Added a benchmark for a set of examples. We measure the time consumption of these examples to use it as a benchmark for future versions of the code. It has been included in the folder **experiments**.

This pull request also closes issue #6 and allows the removal of branch fix_#5 (also deleting the previous pull request #15 ).

commit message:
Added a system to serialize DDRings and DDFunctions

Added a new miscellaneous class (SerializableObject) that provides all
the functionality for serializing (writing on a file) objects. It is
based on the package pickle and save the initialization of an object to
reconstruct it when loaded.

To use this functionality, a class must only inherit from
SerializableObject and initialize the class in the __init__ method
providing the arguments received in the __init__method.

Added the functionaliti of SerializableObject to the classes of the file
ddFunction. Now, DDRings, ParametrizedDDRings and DDFunctions can be
serialized into files.

In particular, the serialization for DDFunctions has an extra parameter
that allows the user to save all the initial conditions that have been
already computed.

Feature/clear sub map

I implemented a SetGridMap service in elevation_mapping to change/process the elevation map from the outside, such that one can feed additional information into elevation mapping (e.g. initializing the elevation map with a ground plane) The changes in grid_map only contain the service definition. The provided map in SetGridMap does not need to be the same resolution, size or position, because the indices are matched through positions. Also, a mask can be, but does not have to be, set for only changing a certain part of the map.

commit message:
Fix for issue #93

While the nodes start up, it can happen that a point cloud arrives that does not find a matching pose. This leads to an Error and confusion of the user. The system starts to work normally once a matching point cloud and pose is available.
An initializing functionality that waits for a matching pair of point cloud and pose is implemented with this commit.\
The user is indicated with a Warn message that initialization is not finished.
The original Error message has been extended for better readability.
Note: robotPoseCache_ does not have a function to check if it is empty.

commit message:
Change ems() 'random' parameter default argument from NULL to ""

The ems() function does not currently behave correctly when the user does
not supply any arguments to the 'random' parameter. The default argument is
NULL. The intention is that this will be interpreted as all factors being
fixed. Instead, it is interpreted as all factors being random. I had not
noticed this before because I pretty much only use ems() as part of the
underlying machinery to my PANGEA shiny app, and the way the function is
called there, an argument is always explicitly passed to 'random' (i.e., if
the user selects all factors fixed, ems is called with random="", rather than
omitting the random parameter). Anyway, the solution appears to be simple:
just change the default argument from NULL to "". That is what this commit
does. It appears to work fine now with this change.

* Update isosurface without creating a new one and more...

This reverts commit 6d87e87b979e86b59b581551dc1e71a306824ee9.

commit message:
Add option to generate primitive surfaces

Feature: Add tess_primitiveShape for generating surface meshes of basic geometric primitives (sphere, box, cylinder, cone, ellipsoid).
This function uses Iso2Mesh to interactively generate triangulated surface meshes for common 3D shapes. It prompts the user for shape-specific parameters and visualizes the resulting mesh. Supports primitive types: sphere, box, cylinder, cone, and ellipsoid. Meshes are cleaned and reoriented, then added to the BST db.
This feature allows the creation and simulation of user-defined electrodes and can be extended for other applications

commit message:
Bugfixes for specparam and SPRiNT

Eliminating bugs in FOOOF and SPRiNT. One bug alters results in extremely rare cases, the other addresses an inconsistency in a data field after post-processing in SPRiNT

specparam and SPRiNT: Adjusted the min/max ranges for peak center frequency to remain in the bounds of model fitting range (e.g., 1-40 Hz). In very rare cases, a peak could be fit with a center frequency outside of the fitting range (e.g., -2 Hz, 42 Hz), even though this output either does not make sense or the data needed to make the claim is not present.

SPRiNT only: Addressed an output update issue where post-processing would update the MSE and R2 of model fits in the stats field, but not the data field (these would remain the same as without post-processing). All fields include data from post-processing only (as long as it was enabled).

author: Diellor Basha <49167439+DiellorBasha@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Add PET volume processing: SUVR, ROI masking, projection to surface (#798)

* Add PETPVE12 plugin support and generalize SPM toolbox linking in bst_plugin

- Added PETPVE12 as a supported plugin in GetSupported(), with download URL, test file, and documentation.
- Extended LinkSpmToolbox (formerly LinkCatSpm) to handle both CAT12 and PETPVE12 using action codes:
    - 0/1/2 for CAT12 (delete/create/check link)
    - 3/4/5 for PETPVE12 (delete/create/check link)
- Updated InstalledFcn, UninstalledFcn, and LoadedFcn for both CAT12 and PETPVE12 to use the new LinkSpmToolbox action codes.
- Ensured plugin installation, linking, and uninstallation workflows are consistent for both toolboxes.
- Maintained backward compatibility for CAT12 and verified no regression/breaking in its functionality.

* Add new function mri_rescale for atlas-based rescaling of intensity values in volume files. Primarily intended for calculating standardized uptake value ratios in PET volumes.

- Rescales volumes by the mean value of a specified ROI from an atlas.
- Supports both file and structure input, with optional subject context for structure input.
- Uses atlas region labels (from bst_get) for robust and consistent ROI selection.
- Handles output as either a new file (with unique file tag inserted before the last underscore-tag) or as a structure.
- Returns atlas labels, output file/struct, error message, and file tag for downstream processing.
- Designed to integrate with mri_mask and Brainstorm's subject/anatomy management.
- Enables flexible atlas-based PET/MRI SUVR normalization.

* Add process_pet  and panel_process_pet for modular PET processing scripting/pipelines

- Iprocess_pet, a pipeline function for PET volume processing, for sequencing atlas-based SUVR rescaling and/or masking in a single workflow.
- process_pet minimizes redundant file saving by chaining operations in memory and saving the final result, with proper file tagging and history.
- Displays the processed PET volume on the subject's default MRI for immediate visualization.
-  panel_process_pet GUI to collect user options and call process_pet, enabling  user-friendly PET processing from the Brainstorm interface.

* Add mri_interp_vol2tess for volume-to-surface projection

-  mri_interp_vol2tess projects MRI/PET/CT volumes onto cortical surfaces (pial, mid, white) using weighted interpolation,
- Enhanced panel_process_pet GUI: added "Project to surface" option
- Updated process_pet pipeline to accept and pass projection command to mri_interp_vol2tess.

* Atlas ROI handling in mri_mask and bst_get

- Added logic in bst_get to retrieve subject's atlas structures, including support for atlas label queries and subject context.
Added a new function, mri_mask, which enables masking of MRI volumes based on existing atlas regions. mri_mask uses atlas label lists from bst_get to obtain ROIs.
- mri_mask supports both file and structure input, outputs the masked MRI (file or struct), the file tag, and the binary mask used.
- mri_mask can be used to list available atlas regions in a given atlas file for the subject, generate a binary mask for a selected region, or save a masked MRI volume to disk, with full subject and atlas context.
- These changes add ROI-based masking functions and flexibility for atlas-based workflows in Brainstorm volumes

* Updated process_pet pipeline to accept and pass projection commandto mri_interp_vol2tess.

* Updated tree_callbacks to inclue PET processing functions: launches GUI for masking, SUVR calculation and surface projection

* Clean up `tree_callbacks`

* Pass `PetFile` instead of `iAnatomy`

* Remove unnecessary function

* Refactor `bst_get('AtlasFile')`

* Refactor `bst_plugin` for SPM Toolboxes

- Same action number regardless the Toolbox

commit message:
Improve iEEG editing features (`Merge electrodes` and `Add/Remove contacts`) (#785)

* Add new feature: Remove selected contact(s)

- Currently supported only for SEEG

- Ways to use:
 * Option-1: Select contact(s) in panel iEEG > press `Delete` or `Backspace`
 * Option-2: Select contact(s) in panel iEEG > click `Contacts (menu) > Remove selected contact(s)`
 * Option-3: Select the contact in 3D figure > press `Delete` or `Backspace`
 * Option-4: Select the contact in 3D figure > right click > `Channels > Remove selected contact(s)`

* If no electrode selected in 3D fig, remove highlight in `panel_ieeg`

* Bugfix: Return if no electrode selected

* Bugfix: Contacts in display in iEEG panel are for the endmost selected electrode

* Ask user to delete whole electrode if all its contacts selected

* Add new feature: Add new contact

- Currently supported only for SEEG

- Ways to use:
 * Option-1: Open 3DViz from SEEG channel > `Add IsoSurface > Select electrode in panel iEEG > Turn on Select Surface Point > Select a location on the IsoSurface > click Contacts (menu) > Add contact`
 * Option-2: Open 3DViz of SEEG channel > `Add IsoSurface > Select electrode in panel iEEG > Turn on Select Surface Point > Select a location on the IsoSurface > Right click (Channels > Add contact)`
 * Option-3: Open MRI Viewer from SEEG channel > `Select electrode in panel iEEG > Set crosshair at a location in MRI Viewer > click Contacts (menu) > Add contact`
 * Option-4: Open MRI Viewer from SEEG channel > Select electrode in panel iEEG > Set crosshair at a location in MRI Viewer > Right click (Electrodes> Add contact)

* Repetition

* Add new feature: Group electrodes

- Currently supported only for SEEG

- Ways to use:
 * Option-1: Select electrodes in panel iEEG > `right click on the electrodes > Group Electrodes`
 * Option-2: Select electrodes in panel iEEG > press `Ctrl+G`

* Some cleanup

* Add shortcut key `S` for `AddContacts`

* Clean

* `GroupElectrodes` is now `MergeElectrodes`; shortcut updated to `CTRL+M`

* `MergeElectrodes`: Remove all to-be-merged electrodes first (non-interactively) and then add new one

* Not required

* Ensure column vector

* Handle case of `'s'` key typed on Contact list

* CTRL+M returns different values in different OS

* Remove `'(s)'`

* Meaningful function name, and variable name

* Remove electrode is interactive if not input arguments

* Remove merged electrodes IFF merge was successful

* Merge validation in merge function not in key shortcut

* Move validation for `AddContact` to function

* Contact list should not warp

* Add "Merge" button

* Simpler `AddContact`

* Select merged electrode when merge is done

* If limited to one Electrode, just work with one electrode

This fix the bug if AddContact is called when >1 selected elect
in this line `SetElectrodes(iSelElec, sSelElec);`

* Checks done where they belong

* Bugfix: `isInteractive` not used anymore

* `figure_3d`: Checks done where they belong

* Uniform naming in menu

* Add appropriate messages

* `AddContact`: Update channel data without using `AlignContacts`

* `MergeContact`: Update channel data without using `AlignContacts`

* Revert `AlignContacts` to original

* Missed typo for `RemoveContact`

* Change scale so that all the menu bar items are visible

* Remove `TODO` comment for ECoG support

Beyond the scope of this PR

* Revert comment for more clarity

It performs more tasks than simple `Delete`

* Remove electrode list panel popup

* Make comment concise

* `RemoveContact`: If limited to one electrode, just work with one electrode

* Bugfix: Find index of channels based on the contact names

* Missed clean up

* Refactor `RemoveContact` to better handle the task

- Encapsulating the entire operation under `isImplantation` to ensure operations are available only for that
- Looping on datasets to delete contacts should be done first followed by looping on datasets to update the contact names in channel

* Comment should describe the big picture, no repeat the line of code

* `RemoveContactHelper` not required

- Do what the function intends to do. If user deletes all contacts for an electrode do not delete the electrode, rather just delete the contacts.
- Number of contacts for an electrode can decrement to 0 if all of them are deleted. Hence the lower limit for this field can go down to 0.

* Handle case where user deletes all but 1 contact and want to `Set skull entry`

* Aligh text

mergemesh merge simply the surfaces and if there are intersection between the surfaces, the volume mesh generation will fail.
mergesurf can handles surface mesh intersection by splitting the intersecting elements and creates new nodes.
with this modification, the volume mesh generation will work.

author: DiellorBasha <diellor.basha@mcgill.ca>
commit message:
Enhanced import_mri function to support PET volume import

This commit modifies the import_mri function to handle PET volumes, including
dynamic PET data with multiple frames. The function now detects PET volumes and
prompts the user to align the frames using SPM, with an optional smoothing step.

Key Enhancements:
- Automatically detects multi-frame (dynamic) PET volumes and sets the registration method to SPM
- Handles dynamic PET volumes by allowing users to:
  - Realign frames using the mri_realign function.
  - Apply optional Gaussian smoothing before importing.
  - Compute the mean volume if realignment is not performed.
- Imports PET data as a single-frame volume if the PET volume is static
- Improved user interactivity through confirmation dialogs.

Future Improvements:
- Add support for Freesurfer registration.
- Enhance user control over smoothing parameters.

during the alignment process. It is designed to handle dynamic PET volumes where
multiple frames are acquired over time.

Key Features:
- Realigns PET frames and computes the average across frames.
- Returns both the realigned  and the computed mean volume.
- Supports optional Gaussian smoothing for enhanced accuracy.

Testing:
- Successfully tested as part of the new import_mri function that supports PET volume import and co-registration

Future Improvements:
- Add support for Freesurfer-based alignment.

dynamic PET data with multiple frames. The function now detects PET volumes and
prompts the user to align the frames using SPM, with an optional smoothing step.

- Handles dynamic PET volumes by allowing users to:
  - Realign frames using the mri_realign function.

- Imports PET data as a single-frame volume if the PET volume is static
- Improved user interactivity through confirmation dialogs.

commit message:
Bugfixes for FOOOF and SPRiNT (#640)

Eliminating bugs in FOOOF and SPRiNT. One bug alters results in extremely rare cases, the other addresses an inconsistency in a data field after post-processing in SPRiNT

specparam and SPRiNT: Adjusted the min/max ranges for peak center frequency to remain in the bounds of model fitting range (e.g., 1-40 Hz). In very rare cases, a peak could be fit with a center frequency outside of the fitting range (e.g., -2 Hz, 42 Hz), even though this output either does not make sense or the data needed to make the claim is not present.

SPRiNT only: Addressed an output update issue where post-processing would update the MSE and R2 of model fits in the stats field, but not the data field (these would remain the same as without post-processing). All fields include data from post-processing only (as long as it was enabled).

Also updates the citation for SPRiNT: doi:10.7554/eLife.77348

Global PCA for scouts and/or unconstrained sources (#559)

* PCA across all files/epochs at once ("global pca") instead of separately for each file ("per-trial PCA"). It applies to extracting scout time-series, either through process_extract_scout or indirectly (e.g. for connectivity on scouts), and to "flattening" unconstrained source orientations to one source per vertex.

* PCA scale change: each scout now more comparable to each other and to mean.

* Connectivity: New option to flatten unconstrained sources with PCA

* Connectivity: Fix scouts on volume and mixed models

commit message:
textured surface handling: allow user to choose from options

The options:

1. Subject has no textured mesh or subject does not exist at all:
 - Import surface GUI pops up, user chooses the surface and it gets loaded
2. Subject already has 1 or more than 1 textured mesh in it then user is given an option:
 - Use existing - if only one mesh present then it just loads that directly; if more than one present then user is given an option to choose which one he wants to use
 - Add New - Import surface GUI pops up, user chooses the surface and it gets loaded
 - Cancel / Press (X) at any instant - cancels the process and exits

commit message:
Add process_pet  and panel_process_pet for modular PET processing scripting/pipelines

- Iprocess_pet, a pipeline function for PET volume processing, for sequencing atlas-based SUVR rescaling and/or masking in a single workflow.
- process_pet minimizes redundant file saving by chaining operations in memory and saving the final result, with proper file tagging and history.
- Displays the processed PET volume on the subject's default MRI for immediate visualization.
-  panel_process_pet GUI to collect user options and call process_pet, enabling  user-friendly PET processing from the Brainstorm interface.

commit message:
Atlas ROI handling in mri_mask and bst_get

- Added logic in bst_get to retrieve subject's atlas structures, including support for atlas label queries and subject context.
Added a new function, mri_mask, which enables masking of MRI volumes based on existing atlas regions. mri_mask uses atlas label lists from bst_get to obtain ROIs.
- mri_mask supports both file and structure input, outputs the masked MRI (file or struct), the file tag, and the binary mask used.
- mri_mask can be used to list available atlas regions in a given atlas file for the subject, generate a binary mask for a selected region, or save a masked MRI volume to disk, with full subject and atlas context.
- These changes add ROI-based masking functions and flexibility for atlas-based workflows in Brainstorm volumes

commit message:
Add new function mri_rescale for atlas-based rescaling of intensity values in volume files. Primarily intended for calculating standardized uptake value ratios in PET volumes.

- Rescales volumes by the mean value of a specified ROI from an atlas.
- Supports both file and structure input, with optional subject context for structure input.
- Uses atlas region labels (from bst_get) for robust and consistent ROI selection.
- Handles output as either a new file (with unique file tag inserted before the last underscore-tag) or as a structure.
- Returns atlas labels, output file/struct, error message, and file tag for downstream processing.
- Designed to integrate with mri_mask and Brainstorm's subject/anatomy management.
- Enables flexible atlas-based PET/MRI SUVR normalization.

commit message:
This commit adds the mri_realign function, which realigns dynamic PET frames
using calls to the SPM batch processing toolbox for PET. The function calculates the mean frame and allows for optional smoothing
during the alignment process. It is designed to handle dynamic PET volumes where
multiple frames are acquired over time.

Key Features:
- Realigns PET frames and computes the average across frames.
- Returns both the realigned  and the computed mean volume.
- Supports optional Gaussian smoothing for enhanced accuracy.

Testing:
- Successfully tested as part of the new import_mri function that supports PET volume import and co-registration

Future Improvements:
- Add support for Freesurfer-based alignment.

commit message:
Visualization tools for FOOOF

Makes use of integrated plotting tools within Brainstorm to plot FOOOF models, as well as aperiodic and peak components separately alongside original PSD files.

- process_fooof.m: added a boolean to future FOOOF_PSD Options struct for identification by panel_display and figure_spectrum.

- bst_memory.m: Added FOOOF-specific fields to be retrieved by in_bst_timefreq.

- db_template.m: Added FOOOF-specific datafields to all future PSDs.

- figure_spectrum.m: Added compatibility with FOOOF data (including full models and separate components), managed by the isFOOOF boolean identifier.

panel_display.m: added FOOOF-specific buttons to appear upon presentation of any PSD (but only enabled by presence of isFOOOF identifier in current figure). Also added another condition specific to FOOOF buttons to determine whether a new display option was selected.

This is a working build, but has not yet been vetted against many bugs, and may not be representative of the intended final build. Will wait to hear what the lab thinks.

commit message:
Waveclus now follows the latest updates from GitHub

We used to use a fixed version of waveclus ever since we first introduced the spikesorter.
Now the updating will be done straight from the latest version of GitHub.

author: langurmonkey <me@tonisagrista.com>
commit message:
build: use externally built JDK for appimage

The JDK in Arch Linux repositories is built against glibc 2.33,
which is cutting edge and not available in most non-rolling distros.
This caused the appimage to not work in these distros. This commit
changes the build system so that an externally built JDK is downloaded,
unpacked and used to build the packaged JRE with `jlink`. We use
the JDK provided by AdoptOpenJDK.

Fixes #361

commit message:
First functional integration with SAMP

This commit contains the first functional integration of Gaia Sky with [SAMP](http://www.ivoa.net/documents/SAMP/).
Since Gaia Sky only displays 3D positional information, and knows how to parse
stars, there are a few restrictions as to how the integration with SAMP is implemneted.

The current implementation only allows using Gaia Sky as a SAMP client. This means that
when Gaia Sky is started, it looks for a preexisting SAMP hub. If it is found, then
a connection is attempted. If it is not found, then Gaia Sky will attempt further
connections in the future using a specified interval of 10 seconds. Gaia Sky will
never run its own SAMP hub, so you will always need a SAMP-hub application (Topcat,
Aladin, etc.) to use the interoperability that SAMP offers.

Also, the only supported format is VOTable. There are, however, some restrictions
as to how the VOTables received through SAMP are interpreted and used (if at all)
by Gaia Sky:

- For the **positional data**, Gaia Sky will look for spherical and cartesian coordinates. In the
case of spherical coordinates, equatorial (`pos.eq.ra`, `pos.eq.dec`), galactic (`pos.galactic.lon`, `pos.galactic.lat`) and
ecliptic (`pos.ecliptic.lon`, `pos.ecliptic.lat`) are supported. To work out the distance, it looks for `pos.parallax` and
`pos.distance`. If either of those are found, they are used. Otherwise, a default parallax of 0.04 mas is used. With
respect to cartesian coordinates, it recognizes `pos.cartesian.x|y|z`, and they are interpreted in the equatorial
system by default.
If no UCDs are available, only equatorial coordinates (ra, dec) are supported, and they are looked up using
the column names.
- **Proper motions** are not yet supported via SAMP.
- **Magnituded** are supported using the `phot.mag` or `phot.mag;stat.mean` UCDs. Otherwise, they are
discovered using the column names `mag`, `bmag`, `gmag`, `phot_g_mean_mag`. If no magnitudes are found,
the default value of 15 is used.
- **Colors** are discovered using the `phot.color` UCD. If not present, the column names `b_v`, `v_i`,
`bp_rp`, `bp_g` and `g_rp` are used, if present. If no color is discovered at all, the default value of 0.656 is used.
- Other physical quantities (mass, flux, T_eff, radius, etc.) are not yet supported via SAMP.

This commit fixes #246

commit message:
feat: add velocity vectors color mode

Three color modes are available:
- 0: direction. In this case, the normalized cartesian velocity components XYZ are directly mapped to the color channels RGB
- 1: speed. In this case, the magnitude of the velocity vector is mapped using a rainbow scheme (blue to green to yellow to red, from small to large) with the maximum at 0.5E8
- 2: radial velocity. Velocity vectors for stars with radial velocities are shown in blue-ish, stars without radial velocities are shown in reddish.

commit message:
Removed libgdx android/html/desktop ifrastructure

- This commit fixes the issue of only a very narrow subset of OpenGL
being available to Gaia Sky because we maintain android and webGL
projects. Not anymore, fortunately.
- Please, note that from this commit on, gaiasky must be run using:

```
 $ gradle core:run
```

- In the same fashion, all gradle tasks which previously required the
`desktop` project keyword now need to use `core` instead.
- `android`, `desktop` and `html` folders removed. `android/assets`
moved to root directory. Everything in `desktop` moved to `core`,
including scripts, libraries and sources.
- Updated all build scripts.
- Fixes #244

author: Volker Gaibler <volker.gaibler@h-its.org>
commit message:
Add REST API for remote control

* Expose scripting API via HTTP
* Basic overview and description given in
  desktop/src/gaia/cu9/ari/gaiaorbit/rest/RESTServer.java
* Implemented using Spark (http://sparkjava.com/documentation.html).
* HTTP method: both GET and POST are supported for ease of use
* Warning: only enable this in a trusted environment
* To enable, set port number to positive value in your
  ~/.gaiasky/global.properties, e.g. program.restport=8080
* Simple functionality check:
  http://localhost:8080/
  shows a greeting page from the REST server.
* Requests now handled with Java reflections, using the formal
  parameter names for better usability. Hence needs to be compiled
  with "-parameters".
* Static files containing examples located below android/assets/rest-static/
  (within class path)

commit message:
perf: improve memory usage of extra star attributes and fix render system
unnecessary `setUniform` calls

This commit defines the extra attributes of stars with a very low
initial capacity (2 versus the default 16) to save memory. Load factor
is slightly increased from default. Additionally, most `setUniform()`
calls happening at renderable level are now sent outside the loop so
that they do not happen as often.

commit message:
feat: add several new functions to enable setting the camera state from
scripts.

- `getObjectPredictedPosition(name)` computes the next-frame position of the object
  identified by `name`. This is useful when the camera position depends
  on the object's.
- `parkCameraRunnable(key, runnable)` enables runnables to run after the
  camera update and between the scene update stages. Use this when
  modifying the camera state.
- `setCamera[Position|Direction|Up](vec, immediate)` are new versions of
  the classical methods to set the position, direction and up vectors of
  the camera, which are applied immediately and not after the current
  frame has finished. Use these if you call them from within a parked
  runnable.

commit message:
Disabled large eye separations in 3D mode

3D mode uses now the approach of updating the scene
once and rendering twice.
This presents problems with large eye separations, due
to the camera being floated, namely:
-  They run into float precision jittering
-  Misdetections in LOD

To fix this we need to either get rid completely of
primitives (points, lines, etc.) and use only triangle
based rendering or do a two step approach where we update
and render the whole scene twice for a single 3D frame. This
second approach would kill the FPS.

object.

commit message:
feat: use XDG base directory structure in Linux

The Linux version now uses the XDG Base Directory Structure, so that
instead of having everything in `~/.gaiasky`, we now have
`~/.local/share/gaiasky` for the data files (scripts, screenshots, data
folder, etc) and `~/.config/gaiasky` for the controller mappings and
config file. You can move the files to the new locations and everything
should just work.
Windows and macOS versions are unaffected by this commit.
